stem:
Bharat has the fraction 2/3 of a chapati. He wants another fraction for the same quantity of that chapati.

Which plan gives an equivalent fraction?

options.text: Change only the numerator to 4 and keep the denominator 3.
Multiply numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number, for example write 4/6.
Write 4/6 even when the new pair is no longer about the same chapati.
First convert 2/3 into a decimal; equivalence requires that conversion.

teacher.key_rationale: An equivalent fraction comes from multiplying or dividing both numerator and denominator by the same nonzero factor, keeping the same quantity of the whole. Changing only the numerator substitutes a one-part edit for that paired change. Dropping the same-whole condition omits what equivalence preserves. Requiring a decimal conversion is outside this hinge.
